skill.name: keyword-research
skill.description: Researches and prioritizes SEO keywords using supplied metrics, search intent, opportunity scoring, GEO signals, and topic clusters.
skill.summary: Builds evidence-labeled keyword priorities and content plans from seed topics and available search data.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, documentation links, and repository metadata. Three findings are confirmed because the instructions execute external Python connectors that contact third-party services. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: External connector commands run scripts outside the reviewed skill files and send query data to third-party services.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before execution, validate arguments, document each destination, and include reviewed connector scripts with the published package.

remediation.issue: The Google Autocomplete helper uses an unofficial endpoint that may create privacy, reliability, or terms-of-service concerns.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the endpoint before use, avoid sensitive queries, apply rate limits, and provide a supported alternative.

content.user_title: Prioritize SEO Keywords and Topic Clusters
content.value_statement: Keyword lists often lack reliable priorities, intent labels, and content direction. This skill scores available data and organizes opportunities into actionable clusters and calendars.
actual_capabilities: Expands seed topics through product, problem, audience, industry, modifier, and long-tail patterns.
Classifies keywords by informational, navigational, commercial, or transactional intent.
Calculates opportunity scores from supplied volume, difficulty, and intent values.
Labels metrics as measured, user-provided, estimated, or unavailable.
Flags question, definition, comparison, list, and how-to queries for GEO planning.
Groups priorities into pillar pages, cluster content, and a recommended publishing calendar.
limitations: It cannot verify search volume or difficulty without connected tools or supplied data.
Model estimates are directional and must not be treated as measured metrics.
Competitor-relative coverage analysis belongs in a separate content-gap workflow.
Optional live-data helpers depend on external services, availability, and usage policies.

use_cases.title: Plan a New SEO Topic
use_cases.description: Turn a seed topic into prioritized keywords, intent groups, and an initial content sequence.

use_cases.title: Find Revenue-Focused Opportunities
use_cases.description: Rank commercial and transactional terms using available demand, difficulty, and business relevance signals.

use_cases.title: Build a Publishable Topic Cluster
use_cases.description: Map a pillar page, supporting articles, internal links, and a practical release cadence.

prompt_templates.title: Expand a Seed Topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Research keywords for [topic] in [market and language]. Group ideas by search intent and label every metric by evidence source.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner keyword discovery from one clear seed.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Product Keywords
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [product or service] for [audience]. Prioritize quick wins, growth terms, and GEO opportunities using my supplied metrics: [metrics].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning with audience and metric context.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Topic Cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a topic cluster for [pillar topic]. Include primary and secondary keywords, intent, content format, internal links, and publishing order.
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured content architecture for an established topic.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Advanced Opportunity Scoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Score these keywords using volume, difficulty, intent, CPC, trend, current rank, and authority: [keyword data]. Explain impact and confidence separately.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prioritization with richer first-party or tool data.

output_examples.input: Research keywords for project management software serving small businesses.
output: Quick win: project management for small teams, commercial intent, with supplied volume 1,200 and difficulty 28.
Pillar: project management for small business. Clusters cover task tracking, remote teams, templates, and software comparisons.
Publish the commercial landing page first, then support it with lower-difficulty instructional articles.

output_examples.input: Prioritize my Search Console queries ranking between positions 5 and 20.
output: First priority: terms with measured impressions, strong business relevance, and positions closest to page one.
Separate optimization candidates from queries requiring new pages.
Mark missing volume or difficulty as unavailable until a trusted source supplies it.

output_examples.input: Build a GEO-focused keyword plan for payroll compliance software.
output: Lead with definitions, jurisdiction comparisons, deadlines, checklists, and concise compliance questions.
Use authoritative sources and structured answers for factual claims.
Connect informational pages to commercial comparison and demo pages through relevant internal links.

best_practices: Provide audience, market, language, business goal, domain strength, and trusted metrics before scoring.
Verify intent against current search results when live data is available.
Refresh priorities quarterly and after meaningful ranking, product, or market changes.
anti_patterns: Do not present inferred volume, difficulty, or trends as measured data.
Do not prioritize high volume without checking intent, relevance, and ranking feasibility.
Do not create thin cluster pages when one stronger page can satisfy the same intent.

faq.question: Does this skill provide live search volume?
faq.answer: Only when a connected source or user-supplied export provides it. Otherwise, volume is unavailable or clearly estimated.

faq.question: How does the skill classify search intent?
faq.answer: It uses query signals and, when available, current search results to assign informational, navigational, commercial, or transactional intent.

faq.question: What is the opportunity score?
faq.answer: It combines volume, intent value, and difficulty to compare keywords. Richer data can add impact and confidence scoring.

faq.question: Can it analyze competitor keyword gaps?
faq.answer: It can use supplied competitor facts, but dedicated competitor-relative coverage gaps require a content-gap analysis workflow.

faq.question: What does GEO opportunity mean?
faq.answer: It identifies queries suited to concise, structured answers, including definitions, comparisons, lists, questions, and how-to content.

faq.question: Can it save the research?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow defines a dated research path and reusable summaries when the host permits filesystem writes.
